newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS - Petronas gets Dai Hung nod, profits jump.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Petronas gets Dai Hung nod, profits jump.

text.p: After announcing a 44.7 percent rise in annual pre-tax profits, Malaysian oil firm Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) said on Monday it had received approval for a Vietnamese offshore oil project.

"We have received approval from Vietnamese authorities on the Dai Hung project and effectively, we are the operator of Dai Hung," Petronas president and chief executive officer Hassan Marican told reporters at a news conference after the release of the results.
Hassan said the state-owned oil firm had taken up the shares in Dai Hung previously owned by Australia's Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP).
Petronas would end up owning around 63.5 percent of Dai Hung, he said.
BHP said in June it had assigned its 43.75 percent stake in the Dai Hung oilfield off the coast of Vietnam to Petronas.
The assignment of the stake in the offshore oil project, effective on December 1, 1996, came after estimates of its reserves gradually fell from 800 million to 100 million barrels.

News of the Vietnamese approval followed the company's announcement that pre-tax profit rose to 12.39 billion ringgit ($4.88 billion) for the year to March 31, 1997, compared to 8.56 billion ringgit in the previous period.

Turnover for the year grew to 28.89 billion ringgit against 22.25 billion ringgit. Petronas said 67.4 percent of the group's turnover was derived from exports of crude oil, refined petroleum products, natural gas, liquefied natural gas and petrochemicals.
The group's sharply higher revenue was the result of "the increase in crude oil price", it said in a statement.
Petronas said Malaysian crude oils for the year to March 31, 1997, averaged $22.29 per barrel, against $18.86 per barrel in 1996.
Hassan said he expected Malaysian crude oil prices to average around $18.00 per barrel for the rest of the year.

A firmer ringgit over the period also contributed to higher earnings in the most recent financial year. Petronas said the ringgit averaged 2.4992 against the dollar over the year under review, compared to 2.5071 the previous year.

The company's 51-percent owned associate, KLCC Holdings Bhd, which developed the Petronas twin-towers in the heart of Kuala Lumpur, could be listed by the end of 1997, said KLCC chairman Azizan Zainol Abidin.
The twin towers, the tallest in the world, form the centre of a 40-hectare (100-acre) site in the centre which will house a mixed residential and commercial development.
Azizan said the share offering would include a foreign tranche. However, he provided no details on the size of the offering, or the proportion of the foreign tranche.
